svg.title: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead of taking anyone's word for it: The build check prints the task a new service is missing, ready to paste
svg.text: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead
of taking anyone's word for it
Scenario: The build check prints the task a new service is missing, ready to paste
A new service without its build task

g.text: Given a generated project adds a frontend service and no task to build it
A project generated by the toolbox. The developer adds a frontend service in a folder of its own, project/frontend, and
writes no task to build it.
git status lists the new Compose file, and cat shows it: one service, frontend, built from its own folder.
When the build check refuses the frontend service and prints the task it
The build check is one of the checks task test runs first. It finds the project's own Compose
file, built by project:build, and the new one, with "Missing task: project:build:frontend".
It fails with the exit code 201, the code Task gives a failed command.
Under the summary, it prints the task to add to project/Taskfile.yml for that service: its
name, project:build:frontend, and the path of its Compose file from the repository root,
Then the task pasted as printed satisfies the build check
The developer pastes those three lines, as printed, at the end of project/Taskfile.yml. git diff shows them under the
The same check now reads "Task found: project:build:frontend" and ends on "All Docker Compose files have an associated
build task!", with the exit code 0.

text.tspan: git diff && task devsecops:test:check:build-coverage; echo "exit code $?"
